It is called the top-open ladder, if {a5 a4 , b5 b4 , a3 a2 , b3 b2 , a1 b1 } ⊆ M (see Figures 7b to 7e). Similar to the case of tower gagdets, we again want to consider well-behaved cycles. Let L be some ladder gagdet. Assume we have some (not necessarily alternating) cycle C in the graph GH , such that C includes at least one vertex of L. The cycle C is called well-behaved for the ladder gadget L, if either • both a0 a1 , b0 b1 ∈ E(C) and both a5 a6 , b5 b6 ̸∈ E(C), or • both a5 a6 , b5 b6 ∈ E(C) and both a0 a1 , b0 b1 ̸∈ E(C). In other words, the cycle C enters the ladder either from the top (i.e. via the edge a5a6 or b5 b6 ) or from the bottom (i.e. via the edge a0 a1 or b0 b1 ), leaves from the the same side it entered, and after that does not visit the inner ladder (vertices ai , bi for i ∈ {1, . . . , 5}) again. In the first case, let us say that the well-behaved cycle C visits L from the top, in the second case, let us say that C visits L from the bottom. The next lemma establishes the already claimed asymmetry, by showing that in order to transform the bottom-open ladder (the top-open ladder, respectively) into the default ladder with well-behaved cycles, we need to primarily come from the bottom (the top, respectively).
